reuse.why: Builds on the existing getRangedScheduleAmount/getScheduledAmount helpers in shared/schedules, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, and the API field calls the same getScheduledAmount the UI uses.

duplication.why: Replaces the inline midpoint in schedule-template and every null/number/range ternary (schedules app, forecast, preview, getScheduledAmount) with one getExpectedScheduleAmount call.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule sits in shared/schedules with the other schedule amount helpers; the API field is computed in the api-models mapping.

scope.why: Only the amount rule, its call sites, the API field and tests/release notes.

maintainability.why: One function owns the rule for every server path and getScheduledAmount delegates to it, but op is optional so the desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount silently keep the exact approximate amount, and a stale 'rounded midpoint' comment remains in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All loot-core amount sites route through getExpectedScheduleAmount (directly or via getScheduledAmount); no copy of the rule remains.

disguised_duplication.where: The per-site dispatches are removed rather than reshaped; getScheduledAmount now delegates to getExpectedScheduleAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedScheduleAmount takes an op with an isapprox branch (step 3), and getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter alongside its inverse flag; no caller re-implements the rule, though the desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount do not pass op.
